title: Quantum-Inspired and Optimization-Based CT Reconstruction Through Spin-Error
authors: Hyunju Lee, Jeonghwa Lee, Yushuang Sam Yang, Clement Chu, Anthony B. Murphy, Kyungtaek Jun
abstract: Quantum-optimization-based computed tomography (CT) reconstruction has demonstrated quantum supremacy in reconstruction accuracy over conventional classical methods under sparse-view and corrupted-sinogram conditions. However, scaling this approach remains challenging because larger images require increasingly many binary variables and interactions in the underlying quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) model. Even with iterative region-of-interest (ROI) refinement, a 60 by 60 ROI with three X-ray mass attenuation coefficients requires 10,800 binary variables under our encoding. As an initial step toward larger quantum CT images, we investigate simulated annealing (SA) followed by spin-error mitigation for optimisation (SEMO), without altering the CT-QUBO objective. We evaluate three 54-view ROI reconstruction instances and nine-view reconstruction with detector-row corruption, comparing SA and SEMO with selected hybrid quantum-classical solver results. For the ROI cases, SEMO reduced the numbers of incorrectly reconstructed pixels in low-budget SA outputs from 13 to 1, 38 to 0, and 54 to 15. With 20 percent detector-row corruption, three of four selected SA and SEMO pairs achieved exact reconstruction. Applying SEMO to one hybrid-solver output reduced its ROI error from 78 to 1 pixel. Improvements were instance-dependent: in one corrupted-sinogram case, QUBO energy decreased while image-domain error increased slightly; in one ROI case, the refined image retained 15 incorrect pixels despite having lower QUBO energy than ground truth. At the evaluated problem sizes, SA and SEMO attained reconstruction accuracy comparable to or better than selected unmitigated hybrid-solver results, providing an initial solution-quality benchmark for future larger-scale, parallelized quantum CT image reconstruction.
summary: This paper investigates using quantum-inspired optimization methods, specifically Simulated Annealing followed by Spin-Error Mitigation (SEMO), to reconstruct CT images. It tackles the scaling challenge of formulating CT as a QUBO problem. The key finding is that SEMO significantly boosts the accuracy of low-budget quantum solver outputs, establishing a strong benchmark for future large-scale quantum medical imaging applications.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of scaling quantum-optimization-based Computed Tomography (CT) reconstruction to larger images by improving current low-budget quantum solver outputs.
main_result: Applying Spin-Error Mitigation for Optimisation (SEMO) significantly improved the reconstruction accuracy of low-budget Simulated Annealing (SA) outputs, achieving results comparable to or better than unmitigated hybrid quantum-classical solvers.
method: The authors use a quantum-inspired approach, formulating CT reconstruction as a QUBO problem, and apply SA followed by SEMO error mitigation to solve it.
model_or_system: The physical system is CT image reconstruction, modeled mathematically as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem derived from sinogram consistency and spatial regularization terms.
key_observables: Reconstruction accuracy, number of incorrectly reconstructed pixels, and QUBO energy.
important_parameters: The problem size is benchmarked at a $60 	imes 60$ ROI, which translates to 10,800 binary variables; scaling to larger images is the long-term goal.
main_assumptions: The study assumes that SA-SEMO can provide a reliable initial solution-quality benchmark, although it does not guarantee reaching the true global QUBO optimum.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the paper compares SA-SEMO results against hybrid-solver outputs for various ROI and corrupted-sinogram test cases.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the QUBO formulation for CT reconstruction, then details the use of SA and SEMO for solving this problem, and finally presents comparative results across various test instances (ROI and corrupted sinograms) to benchmark the mitigation technique.
why_interesting: The work directly applies quantum optimization techniques (QUBO, SA, SEMO) to a complex inverse problem in medical imaging, providing a concrete, near-term application case for quantum computation.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Comparison of ground-truth images, low-budget simulated annealing (SA) reconstructions, and SEMO- mitigated reconstructions for three 54-view ROI-QCSTR instances. The initial SA setting was fixed at 20 reads, 50 sweeps, and random seed 42 for all three instances. The number of incorrectly reconstructed pixels is indicated for each reconstructed image.

Figure 2. SEMO error mitigation in the ring-artifact reconstruction experiment with 15% projection sampling and 20% detector-row corruption. The upper row shows the full-view sinogram with 60 views, the sparse sinogram generated from nine uniformly spaced projection angles (15% of the 60-view reference angular count), and the corresponding corrupted sinogram. The lower row shows the ground-truth image, the low-budget SA reconstruction, and the SEMO-mitigated reconstruction. The number of incorrectly reconstructed pixels decreased from 38 to zero after SEMO processing.

Figure 3. QUBO energy and MAE improvements after SEMO processing for the main ROI-QCSTR and ring- artifact experiments. The horizontal axis represents the reduction in QUBO energy, ∆𝑬= 𝑬𝐛𝐞𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐞−𝑬𝐚𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫, and the vertical axis represents the reduction in mean absolute error, ∆𝑴𝑨𝑬= 𝑴𝑨𝑬𝐛𝐞𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐞−𝑴𝑨𝑬𝐚𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫 . Positive values on both axes indicate simultaneous improvement in the QUBO objective and image-domain reconstruction accuracy. The symbol × 𝟐 indicates two evaluated runs with identical (∆𝑬,∆𝑴𝑨𝑬) coordinates.
